blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal.

blocks.text: Lots and land in East Burnaby

items.t: Established-street house lots: predominantly freehold detached on the interior streets in this row, with strata product at the edges toward Edmonds and New Westminster; the exact split by street is not verified.

Lot character: typical lot sizes are not verified at sub-area level — no official source read states them. The only sourced size figures are the R1 SSMUH thresholds in (280 m² / 281 m²), which are zoning thresholds, not a claim about any existing lot's size.

Serviced position: Burnaby's 2026 residential utility notice covers annual water, annual sewer use, a cross-connection device charge where applicable and a garbage toter fee, with the detached single-family water charge at $652.33 and sewer for single-family homes billed as a sewer parcel tax — the established streets sit inside that municipal system on the City's wording; servicing for any single parcel is confirmed with the City, not confirmed parcel-by-parcel here.
ALR vs non-ALR: no ALR parcel in East Burnaby is confirmed; ALR status is a property-specific check through the Agricultural Land Commission. No ALR percentage split is stated.

Park- and creek-edge diligence: creeks and streams run through Robert Burnaby Park and the ravine lands on the east side, and the City's restoration project is removing invasive species and planting 3,000 new trees with some trails and areas closed during the work; a floodplain designation for the residential streets was not confirmed in the sources read. Parcel-level hazard and watercourse-setback status are property-specific checks.

Burnaby Housing Authority — 10th Avenue and Newcombe Street (New Westminster edge). REZONING APPLICATION, rental, excluded from every count: the Burnaby Housing Authority (a municipal corporation established by the City of Burnaby) has submitted a rezoning application for a property at 10th Avenue and Newcombe Street with plans for 204 new affordable and market rental homes in two six-storey buildings with patios, community gardens and landscaped green spaces. Purpose-built rental by application — nothing here is a lot, a strata unit or a presale offering on this evidence.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around East Burnaby

items.t: East Burnaby is a City of Burnaby GVR board sub-area covering the eastern quadrant — from the Edmonds town centre and the Kingsway / Canada Way corridors east to the City of New Westminster border, taking in the Cariboo-Armstrong streets, the Second Street and Twelfth Avenue school neighbourhoods and the Robert Burnaby Park lands. Boundaries: Not verified — no City source read publishes street-by-street boundaries for the MLS sub-area, and which east-side schools fall inside the MLS line versus the Edmonds and Cariboo lines is not verified.
Nearby areas: Edmonds and Highgate west and south-west, Cariboo and The Crest within the east side, South Slope south-west, and the City of New Westminster across 10th Avenue / the eastern border.

Main roads: Canada Way, Kingsway, Edmonds Street and 10th Avenue east–west, with 6th Street, 2nd Street and Cariboo Road running north–south toward Lougheed Highway and New Westminster. Transit: Edmonds Station (Expo Line) serves the west side; route 116 runs between Metrotown Station and Edmonds Station via Imperial, Sussex, Marine Drive, Marine Way, Byrne Road, Southridge Drive, Griffiths Drive and 18th Avenue. Commute times in minutes: Not verified.

Civic anchors: Robert Burnaby Park (creeks and streams throughout, over half its area critical wildlife habitat; 3 tennis courts and 10 pickleball courts with a practice wall); Rosemary Brown Recreation Centre, 7789 18th Street (2 NHL-sized rinks); Edmonds Community Centre, 7433 Edmonds Street, at the west edge; Tommy Douglas Library is the branch serving this quadrant. Nearest hospital: Burnaby Hospital, 3935 Kincaid St, north-west across the city; Edmonds Urgent and Primary Care Centre at #201-7315 Edmonds St, at the west side.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in East Burnaby

items.t: Habitat diligence: over half of Robert Burnaby Park is critical wildlife habitat and restoration work runs through it — for park- and creek-edge lots, check watercourse setbacks and the restoration project's trail closures early.

ALR rules (for completeness — no East Burnaby ALR parcel is confirmed here): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s. 6; SPA s. 239; ALCA s. 21(1)); ALC residence caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha). Farm class is three-tiered ($2,500 on 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 + 5% of value over 4 ha; $10,000 under 0.8 ha; applications by Oct 31) — a flat "$2,500+" line is an ERROR.

blocks.text: Good to know about East Burnaby

items.t: The quadrant is being replanted while you buy in it: the City's Robert Burnaby Park restoration removes invasive species and plants 3,000 new trees, with some trails and areas closed during the work — a park-edge lot's outlook and access change over the project, in the improving direction, on the City's own description.

The east side's newest plan layer is dated March 2025: the Edmonds Community Plan was officially adopted that month for the town-centre part of the quadrant, and the Burnaby 2050 OCP (adopted December 9, 2025) now takes precedence over older community-plan maps where they conflict — check both layers for a town-centre-edge lot.

The City is its own landlord at the border: the 204-home project at 10th Avenue and Newcombe Street is the Burnaby Housing Authority's application — a municipal corporation's rental project, part of a two-project announcement totalling 387 new rental homes — so the quadrant's most visible "new development" adds rental supply, not purchasable land or strata.

faq.q: Is there a vacant lot subdivision in East Burnaby?
faq.a: No bare-land subdivision or presale lot offering was verified.

faq.q: Can an East Burnaby house lot add units — and can they be strata?
faq.a: Under the R1 SSMUH District: 3 units on lots up to 280 m², 4 units on larger lots, 6 units on lots of at least 281 m² within 400 m of a frequent-transit stop — and lots with two or more primary units may be stratified. Confirm the parcel's district and transit distance with the City.

faq.q: What checks does a Robert Burnaby Park-edge lot need?
faq.a: Watercourse-setback and habitat checks, early — many creeks run through the park, over half of it is critical wildlife habitat, and restoration closures run through it; no floodplain designation for the residential streets was confirmed, so the position is parcel-specific.

Burnaby's eastern quadrant — the residential east side between the Edmonds town centre and the New Westminster border, taking in Robert Burnaby Park, Cariboo Hill and the Second Street and Twelfth Avenue neighbourhoods; it is a GVR MLS® sub-area name, not one small neighbourhood.

faq.q: Which schools are on Burnaby's east side?
faq.a: SD41 schools on the Province's list include Second Street Community Elementary (K–7), 7502 2nd St, Twelfth Avenue Elementary (K–7), 7622 12th Ave, Taylor Park Elementary (K–7), 7590 Mission Ave, and Cariboo Hill Secondary (8–12), 8580 16th Ave; catchments are address-based and must be checked in the SD41 locator.

The east side's large forested park — the City describes many creeks and streams running through it and over half its area as critical wildlife habitat, and is restoring it with invasive-species removal and 3,000 new trees; its courts are listed at 3 tennis and 10 pickleball.
